Campos is one of more than 50 people who have died in ICE custody since January 2025, the deadliest stretch for immigration detention on record. The report connects these deaths to a rapid, unchecked expansion of detention.
The report takes its title from what a guard told one detained man. You're only getting out deported or dead. That line captures how people inside describe the place.

In January, Geraldo Lunas Campos, a 55-year-old Cuban man, died at the facility. The medical examiner ruled his death a homicide caused by asphyxia from neck and torso compression. Witnesses say he told guards, I can't breathe.
More than 60 people reported that the facility denied or delayed their medication. Diabetics went without consistent insulin. People with serious conditions waited weeks to see a doctor.
People reported six toilets and showers shared among 72 detainees in a single pod, bathrooms left filthy for weeks, and food portions so small that some said they lost up to 30 pounds.
64 of the 80 people interviewed said they were beaten or saw others beaten. They described groups of 10 to 20 guards in riot gear beating detainees during hunger strikes and protests over conditions.

Human Rights Watch and the ACLU spent eight months investigating Camp East Montana at Fort Bliss, the largest immigration detention facility in US history. They documented beatings, medical neglect, and squalid conditions. 🧵

He is the 50th person to die in ICE detention under this administration. By my count, 60 people have died in or connected to ICE enforcement since January 2025.

He was held at Irwin County Detention Center, which ICE reopened last fall after shutting it in 2021 over allegations a gynecologist performed unnecessary procedures, including hysterectomies, on detained women.

His sister says ICE ignored the family's request that he bring his medication and let him take only one of the drugs he needed. He called her from detention to say he still wasn't getting it. The GBI is now investigating.
He had been in custody four days. ICE arrested him at his home on July 9. By July 13 he was dead. His suspected cause of death is cardiac arrest, with the official cause still pending.

Jesús Manuel Arenas-Silva, 45, from Venezuela, died in ICE custody on July 13. He was on a bus between two Georgia detention centers when staff found him unresponsive. He is the 22nd person to die in ICE custody in 2026.
